title: PowerPoint on the web: reference a Teams meeting or chat when creating a presentation with Copilot Agent Mode
summary: Hold: Microsoft documents that sensitivity labels protecting Teams meetings and chat are not inherited by Copilot-generated destination content, rather than leaving this unanswered. The default field also understates the documented user-initiated capability; the licence-assignment path and PowerShell call are supported.

claims.claim: This feature references Teams meetings or chats when creating a presentation with Agent Mode in PowerPoint.
claims.quote: You can now reference a Teams meeting or chat when creating a presentation with Agent Mode in PowerPoint.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Scope; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Users mention a Teams meeting or chat in a prompt and Copilot generates a deck based on that content.
claims.quote: Users can enter a prompt that mentions the relevant Teams meeting or chat, and Copilot will generate a deck based on that content.

claims.claim: The release notes instruct the user to press Enter to create the presentation.
claims.quote: Press Enter. Copilot will create a presentation using the referenced Teams content.

claims.claim: The release notes list this feature under July 01, 2026, differing from the roadmap target.
claims.quote:
## July 01, 2026
### PowerPoint
Reference a Teams meeting or chat when creating a presentation with Agent Mode in PowerPoint [Windows, Web, Mac]

claims.claim: Learn has no dedicated feature page beyond the release-notes entry.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot PowerPoint Agent Mode reference Teams meeting chat; "PowerPoint" "Teams meeting or chat" transcript recap matching. Read release notes; results concerned Teams policies, recap or agents in the Copilot app, not a dedicated page for this feature.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Copilot surfaces only organisational data the individual user has at least view permissions to, preserving existing access boundaries.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot only surfaces organizational data to which individual users have at least view permissions.

claims.claim: Copilot honours user usage rights on data encrypted by Microsoft Purview Information Protection, through sensitivity labels or restricted permissions.
claims.quote: When you have data that's encrypted by Microsoft Purview Information Protection, Microsoft Copilot honors the usage rights granted to the user. This encryption can be applied by sensitivity labels or by restricted permissions in apps in Microsoft 365

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether generated decks inherit the sensitivity label of a source Teams meeting or chat.
claims.quote: Sensitivity labels that protect Teams meetings and chat aren't currently recognized by Copilot and agents. For example, data returned from a meeting chat or channel chat won't display an associated sensitivity label
claims.fix: Replace the label-inheritance absence and that part of the open question with: 'Microsoft documents that Copilot does not recognize sensitivity labels protecting Teams meetings and chat: returned chat data does not display the label, copying it to a destination item cannot be prevented, and the label cannot be inherited. This limitation does not apply to labelled meeting invites, responses or calendar events.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/ai-m365-copilot-considerations.

claims.claim: The feature documentation describes no new identity or permission model.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot PowerPoint Agent Mode reference Teams meeting chat; PowerPoint Agent Mode reference Teams meeting chat tenant admin switch default rollout setting. Read release-notes entry and Copilot privacy page; neither describes a new identity model for this feature.

claims.claim: No documentation found describes this feature taking actions outside the presentation.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot PowerPoint Agent Mode reference Teams meeting chat. Read release-notes entry: its instructions describe creating a presentation. Results for agents in the Copilot app do not establish additional actions for Agent Mode inside PowerPoint.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published how a referenced meeting or chat is matched to the prompt.
claims.quote: Searched: "PowerPoint" "Teams meeting or chat" transcript recap matching; "PowerPoint" "Teams meeting" "prompt" matching meeting chat. Read release-notes entry; it instructs users to reference the meeting or chat but supplies no matching algorithm.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The mixed product-level entitlement is Microsoft 365 E7 inclusion or an add-on for eligible commercial, US Government and education plans.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot is available with Microsoft 365 E7 or as an add-on for eligible commercial, US Government, and education subscription plans.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: No feature-specific licence rule was found, including for Copilot Chat users without a Microsoft Copilot licence.
claims.quote: Searched: "PowerPoint" "Agent Mode" "Teams" "license"; "PowerPoint" "Agent Mode" licensing Copilot Chat meter admin control. Read Copilot licensing and release notes. Paid-licence results concern PowerPoint Agents in the Copilot app, not this in-app Teams-reference feature.

claims.claim: No separate meter or charge for this feature is published in the cited licensing page or release-notes entry.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Agent Mode Teams referencing pricing consumption meter charge licensing. Read Copilot licensing and release-notes entry; neither names a separate meter or charge. Search results describe other products' meters, not this feature.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Licence assignment requires at least License Administrator or User Administrator.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.

claims.claim: General user licence assignment is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses.
claims.quote: In the admin center, go to the Users > Active users page. Select the row of the user that you want to assign a license to. In the right pane, select Licenses and Apps. Expand the Licenses section, select the boxes for the licenses that you want to assign

claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @() assigns a licence through Microsoft Graph PowerShell.
claims.quote:
To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell.
Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: The release notes state no feature-specific prerequisite, and a transcript or recap requirement for this feature was not found.
claims.quote: Searched: "PowerPoint" "Teams meeting or chat" transcript recap matching. Read release-notes entry. Results state requirements for Teams recap, Teams meeting Copilot or Sales agents, not for referencing a meeting in PowerPoint Agent Mode.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The default state is unknown despite the documented capability that users choose by naming a meeting or chat in a prompt.
claims.quote: Users can enter a prompt that mentions the relevant Teams meeting or chat, and Copilot will generate a deck based on that content.
claims.fix: Set defaultState to 'user-opt-in', as the standard defines an available capability each user chooses to use after a search finds no feature-specific admin switch. Replace the first sentence of the second Why it matters paragraph with: 'Users choose to use the capability by referencing a Teams meeting or chat in a prompt; no feature-specific admin switch is documented at the time of writing (November 2026).' Retain action 'review'.

claims.claim: No feature-specific administrator switch is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "PowerPoint" "Agent Mode" "Teams" Graph PowerShell disable setting; PowerPoint Agent Mode reference Teams meeting chat tenant admin switch default rollout setting. Read release notes and privacy; returned Teams policies and Copilot-app agent controls do not name this feature.

claims.claim: The user's existing Teams and file access permissions govern the data Copilot can surface.
claims.quote: It's important that you're using the permission models available in Microsoft 365 services, such as SharePoint, to help ensure the right users or groups have the right access to the right content within your organization.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The checklist asks readers to review Teams access and oversharing, but the controls table has only licence assignment.
claims.quote: Review oversharing in Teams chats and channels that licensed users can read ... Which users hold a Microsoft Copilot licence ... Teams and file permissions ... not in this table.
claims.fix: Remove the Before rollout bullet 'Review oversharing in Teams chats and channels that licensed users can read, because Copilot results follow what each user has at least view permissions to.' It asks for a review of a control missing from the table; do not add an unverified row.

claims.claim: Microsoft names no feature-specific administrator action.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Agent Mode reference Teams meeting chat tenant admin switch default rollout setting. Read release-notes entry and Copilot licensing: the entry gives user instructions; licensing gives general product setup, not a feature-specific administrator action.
